topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 1
text: To construct an equilateral triangle on a given finite straight line.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 2
text: To place a straight line equal to a given straight line with one end at a given point.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 3
text: To cut off from the greater of two given unequal straight lines a straight line equal to the less.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 4
text: If two triangles have two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have the angles contained by the equal straight lines equal, then they also have the base equal to the base, the triangle equals the triangle, and the remaining angles equal the remaining angles respectively, namely those opposite the equal sides.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 5
text: In isosceles triangles the angles at the base equal one another, and, if the equal straight lines are produced further, then the angles under the base equal one another.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 6
text: If in a triangle two angles equal one another, then the sides opposite the equal angles also equal one another.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 7
text: Given two straight lines constructed from the ends of a straight line and meeting in a point, there cannot be constructed from the ends of the same straight line, and on the same side of it, two other straight lines meeting in another point and equal to the former two respectively, namely each equal to that from the same end.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 8
text: If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and also have the base equal to the base, then they also have the angles equal which are contained by the equal straight lines.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 9
text: To bisect a given rectilinear angle.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 10
text: To bisect a given finite straight line.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 11
text: To draw a straight line at right angles to a given straight line from a given point on it.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 12
text: To draw a straight line perpendicular to a given infinite straight line from a given point not on it.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 13
text: If a straight line stands on a straight line, then it makes either two right angles or angles whose sum equals two right angles.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 14
text: If with any straight line, and at a point on it, two straight lines not lying on the same side make the sum of the adjacent angles equal to two right angles, then the two straight lines are in a straight line with one another.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 15
text: If two straight lines cut one another, then they make the vertical angles equal to one another.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 16
text: In any triangle, if one of the sides is produced, then the exterior angle is greater than either of the interior and opposite angles.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 17
text: In any triangle the sum of any two angles is less than two right angles.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 18
text: In any triangle the angle opposite the greater side is greater.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 19
text: In any triangle the side opposite the greater angle is greater.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 20
text: In any triangle the sum of any two sides is greater than the remaining one.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 21
text: If from the ends of one of the sides of a triangle two straight lines are constructed meeting within the triangle, then the sum of the straight lines so constructed is less than the sum of the remaining two sides of the triangle, but the constructed straight lines contain a greater angle than the angle contained by the remaining two sides.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 22
text: To construct a triangle out of three straight lines which equal three given straight lines: thus it is necessary that the sum of any two of the straight lines should be greater than the remaining one.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 23
text: To construct a rectilinear angle equal to a given rectilinear angle on a given straight line and at a point on it.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 24
text: If two triangles have two sides equal to two sides respectively, but have one of the angles contained by the equal straight lines greater than the other, then they also have the base greater than the base.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 25
text: If two triangles have two sides equal to two sides respectively, but have the base greater than the base, then they also have the one of the angles contained by the equal straight lines greater than the other.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 26
text: If two triangles have two angles equal to two angles respectively, and one side equal to one side, namely, either the side adjoining the equal angles, or that opposite one of the equal angles, then the remaining sides equal the remaining sides and the remaining angle equals the remaining angle.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 27
text: If a straight line falling on two straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one another, then the straight lines are parallel to one another.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 28
text: If a straight line falling on two straight lines makes the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle on the same side, or the sum of the interior angles on the same side equal to two right angles, then the straight lines are parallel to one another.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 29
text: A straight line falling on parallel straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one another, the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle, and the sum of the interior angles on the same side equal to two right angles.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 30
text: Straight lines parallel to the same straight line are also parallel to one another.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 31
text: To draw a straight line through a given point parallel to a given straight line.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 32
text: In any triangle, if one of the sides is produced, then the exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior and opposite angles, and the sum of the three interior angles of the triangle equals two right angles.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 33
text: Straight lines which join the ends of equal and parallel straight lines in the same directions are themselves equal and parallel.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 34
text: In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles equal one another, and the diameter bisects the areas.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 35
text: Parallelograms which are on the same base and in the same parallels equal one another.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 36
text: Parallelograms which are on equal bases and in the same parallels equal one another.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 37
text: Triangles which are on the same base and in the same parallels equal one another.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 38
text: Triangles which are on equal bases and in the same parallels equal one another.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 39
text: Equal triangles which are on the same base and on the same side are also in the same parallels.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 40
text: Equal triangles which are on equal bases and on the same side are also in the same parallels.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 41
text: If a parallelogram has the same base with a triangle and is in the same parallels, then the parallelogram is double the triangle.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 42
text: To construct a parallelogram equal to a given triangle in a given rectilinear angle.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 43
text: In any parallelogram the complements of the parallelograms about the diameter equal one another.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 44
text: To a given straight line in a given rectilinear angle, to apply a parallelogram equal to a given triangle.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 45
text: To construct a parallelogram equal to a given rectilinear figure in a given rectilinear angle.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 46
text: To describe a square on a given straight line.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 47
text: In right-angled triangles the square on the side opposite the right angle equals the sum of the squares on the sides containing the right angle.

topic: Book I: Triangles, parallels and area
title: Book I, Proposition 48
text: If in a triangle the square on one of the sides equals the sum of the squares on the remaining two sides of the triangle, then the angle contained by the remaining two sides of the triangle is right.

title: Book II, Proposition 1
text: If there are two straight lines, and one of them is cut into any number of segments whatever, then the rectangle contained by the two straight lines equals the sum of the rectangles contained by the uncut straight line and each of the segments.

title: Book II, Proposition 2
text: If a straight line is cut at random, then the sum of the rectangles contained by the whole and each of the segments equals the square on the whole.

title: Book II, Proposition 3
text: If a straight line is cut at random, then the rectangle contained by the whole and one of the segments equals the sum of the rectangle contained by the segments and the square on the aforesaid segment.

title: Book II, Proposition 4
text: If a straight line is cut at random, the square on the whole equals the squares on the segments plus twice the rectangle contained by the segments.

title: Book II, Proposition 5
text: If a straight line is cut into equal and unequal segments, then the rectangle contained by the unequal segments of the whole together with the square on the straight line between the points of section equals the square on the half.

title: Book II, Proposition 6
text: If a straight line is bisected and a straight line is added to it in a straight line, then the rectangle contained by the whole with the added straight line and the added straight line together with the square on the half equals the square on the straight line made up of the half and the added straight line.

title: Book II, Proposition 7
text: If a straight line is cut at random, then the sum of the square on the whole and that on one of the segments equals twice the rectangle contained by the whole and the said segment plus the square on the remaining segment.

title: Book II, Proposition 8
text: If a straight line is cut at random, then four times the rectangle contained by the whole and one of the segments plus the square on the remaining segment equals the square described on the whole and the aforesaid segment as on one straight line.

title: Book II, Proposition 9
text: If a straight line is cut into equal and unequal segments, then the sum of the squares on the unequal segments of the whole is double the sum of the square on the half and the square on the straight line between the points of section.

title: Book II, Proposition 10
text: If a straight line is bisected, and a straight line is added to it in a straight line, then the square on the whole with the added straight line and the square on the added straight line both together are double the sum of the square on the half and the square described on the straight line made up of the half and the added straight line as on one straight line.

title: Book II, Proposition 11
text: To cut a given straight line so that the rectangle contained by the whole and one of the segments equals the square on the remaining segment.

title: Book II, Proposition 12
text: In obtuse-angled triangles the square on the side opposite the obtuse angle is greater than the sum of the squares on the sides containing the obtuse angle by twice the rectangle contained by one of the sides about the obtuse angle, namely that on which the perpendicular falls, and the straight line cut off outside by the perpendicular towards the obtuse angle.

title: Book II, Proposition 13
text: In acute-angled triangles the square on the side opposite the acute angle is less than the sum of the squares on the sides containing the acute angle by twice the rectangle contained by one of the sides about the acute angle, namely that on which the perpendicular falls, and the straight line cut off within by the perpendicular towards the acute angle.

title: Book II, Proposition 14
text: To construct a square equal to a given rectilinear figure.

title: Book III, Proposition 1
text: To find the center of a given circle.

title: Book III, Proposition 2
text: If two points are taken at random on the circumference of a circle, then the straight line joining the points falls within the circle.

title: Book III, Proposition 3
text: If a straight line passing through the center of a circle bisects a straight line not passing through the center, then it also cuts it at right angles; and if it cuts it at right angles, then it also bisects it.

title: Book III, Proposition 4
text: If in a circle two straight lines which do not pass through the center cut one another, then they do not bisect one another.

title: Book III, Proposition 5
text: If two circles cut one another, then they do not have the same center.

title: Book III, Proposition 6
text: If two circles touch one another, then they do not have the same center.

title: Book III, Proposition 7
text: If on the diameter of a circle a point is taken which is not the center of the circle, and from the point straight lines fall upon the circle, then that is greatest on which passes through the center, the remainder of the same diameter is least, and of the rest the nearer to the straight line through the center is always greater than the more remote; and only two equal straight lines fall from the point on the circle, one on each side of the least straight line.

title: Book III, Proposition 8
text: If a point is taken outside a circle and from the point straight lines are drawn through to the circle, one of which is through the center and the others are drawn at random, then, of the straight lines which fall on the concave circumference, that through the center is greatest, while of the rest the nearer to that through the center is always greater than the more remote, but, of the straight lines falling on the convex circumference, that between the point and the diameter is least, while of the rest the nearer to the least is always less than the more remote; and only two equal straight lines fall on the circle from the point, one on each side of the least.

title: Book III, Proposition 9
text: If a point is taken within a circle, and more than two equal straight lines fall from the point on the circle, then the point taken is the center of the circle.

title: Book III, Proposition 10
text: A circle does not cut a circle at more than two points.

title: Book III, Proposition 11
text: If two circles touch one another internally, and their centers are taken, then the straight line joining their centers, being produced, falls on the point of contact of the circles.

title: Book III, Proposition 12
text: If two circles touch one another externally, then the straight line joining their centers passes through the point of contact.

title: Book III, Proposition 13
text: A circle does not touch another circle at more than one point whether it touches it internally or externally..

title: Book III, Proposition 14
text: Equal straight lines in a circle are equally distant from the center, and those which are equally distant from the center equal one another.

title: Book III, Proposition 15
text: Of straight lines in a circle the diameter is greatest, and of the rest the nearer to the center is always greater than the more remote.

title: Book III, Proposition 16
text: The straight line drawn at right angles to the diameter of a circle from its end will fall outside the circle, and into the space between the straight line and the circumference another straight line cannot be interposed, further the angle of the semicircle is greater, and the remaining angle less, than any acute rectilinear angle.

title: Book III, Proposition 17
text: From a given point to draw a straight line touching a given circle.

title: Book III, Proposition 18
text: If a straight line touches a circle, and a straight line is joined from the center to the point of contact, the straight line so joined will be perpendicular to the tangent.

title: Book III, Proposition 19
text: If a straight line touches a circle, and from the point of contact a straight line is drawn at right angles to the tangent, the center of the circle will be on the straight line so drawn.

title: Book III, Proposition 20
text: In a circle the angle at the center is double the angle at the circumference when the angles have the same circumference as base.

title: Book III, Proposition 21
text: In a circle the angles in the same segment equal one another.

title: Book III, Proposition 22
text: The sum of the opposite angles of quadrilaterals in circles equals two right angles.

title: Book III, Proposition 23
text: On the same straight line there cannot be constructed two similar and unequal segments of circles on the same side.

title: Book III, Proposition 24
text: Similar segments of circles on equal straight lines equal one another.

title: Book III, Proposition 25
text: Given a segment of a circle, to describe the complete circle of which it is a segment.

title: Book III, Proposition 26
text: In equal circles equal angles stand on equal circumferences whether they stand at the centers or at the circumferences.

title: Book III, Proposition 27
text: In equal circles angles standing on equal circumferences equal one another whether they stand at the centers or at the circumferences.

title: Book III, Proposition 28
text: In equal circles equal straight lines cut off equal circumferences, the greater circumference equals the greater and the less equals the less.

title: Book III, Proposition 29
text: In equal circles straight lines that cut off equal circumferences are equal.

title: Book III, Proposition 30
text: To bisect a given circumference.

title: Book III, Proposition 31
text: In a circle the angle in the semicircle is right, that in a greater segment less than a right angle, and that in a less segment greater than a right angle; further the angle of the greater segment is greater than a right angle, and the angle of the less segment is less than a right angle.

title: Book III, Proposition 32
text: If a straight line touches a circle, and from the point of contact there is drawn across, in the circle, a straight line cutting the circle, then the angles which it makes with the tangent equal the angles in the alternate segments of the circle.

title: Book III, Proposition 33
text: On a given straight line to describe a segment of a circle admitting an angle equal to a given rectilinear angle.

title: Book III, Proposition 34
text: From a given circle to cut off a segment admitting an angle equal to a given rectilinear angle.

title: Book III, Proposition 35
text: If in a circle two straight lines cut one another, then the rectangle contained by the segments of the one equals the rectangle contained by the segments of the other.

title: Book III, Proposition 36
text: If a point is taken outside a circle and two straight lines fall from it on the circle, and if one of them cuts the circle and the other touches it, then the rectangle contained by the whole of the straight line which cuts the circle and the straight line intercepted on it outside between the point and the convex circumference equals the square on the tangent.

title: Book III, Proposition 37
text: If a point is taken outside a circle and from the point there fall on the circle two straight lines, if one of them cuts the circle, and the other falls on it, and if further the rectangle contained by the whole of the straight line which cuts the circle and the straight line intercepted on it outside between the point and the convex circumference equals the square on the straight line which falls on the circle, then the straight line which falls on it touches the circle.

title: Book IV, Proposition 11

title: Book IV, Proposition 12

title: Book IV, Proposition 13

title: Book IV, Proposition 14

title: Book V, Proposition 1
text: If any number of magnitudes are each the same multiple of the same number of other magnitudes, then the sum is that multiple of the sum.

title: Book V, Proposition 2
text: If a first magnitude is the same multiple of a second that a third is of a fourth, and a fifth also is the same multiple of the second that a sixth is of the fourth, then the sum of the first and fifth also is the same multiple of the second that the sum of the third and sixth is of the fourth.

title: Book V, Proposition 3
text: If a first magnitude is the same multiple of a second that a third is of a fourth, and if equimultiples are taken of the first and third, then the magnitudes taken also are equimultiples respectively, the one of the second and the other of the fourth.

title: Book V, Proposition 4
text: If a first magnitude has to a second the same ratio as a third to a fourth, then any equimultiples whatever of the first and third also have the same ratio to any equimultiples whatever of the second and fourth respectively, taken in corresponding order.

title: Book V, Proposition 5
text: If a magnitude is the same multiple of a magnitude that a subtracted part is of a subtracted part, then the remainder also is the same multiple of the remainder that the whole is of the whole.

title: Book V, Proposition 6
text: If two magnitudes are equimultiples of two magnitudes, and any magnitudes subtracted from them are equimultiples of the same, then the remainders either equal the same or are equimultiples of them.

title: Book V, Proposition 7
text: Equal magnitudes have to the same the same ratio; and the same has to equal magnitudes the same ratio.

title: Book V, Proposition 8
text: Of unequal magnitudes, the greater has to the same a greater ratio than the less has; and the same has to the less a greater ratio than it has to the greater.

title: Book V, Proposition 9
text: Magnitudes which have the same ratio to the same equal one another; and magnitudes to which the same has the same ratio are equal.

title: Book V, Proposition 10
text: Of magnitudes which have a ratio to the same, that which has a greater ratio is greater; and that to which the same has a greater ratio is less.

title: Book V, Proposition 11
text: Ratios which are the same with the same ratio are also the same with one another.

title: Book V, Proposition 12
text: If any number of magnitudes are proportional, then one of the antecedents is to one of the consequents as the sum of the antecedents is to the sum of the consequents.

title: Book V, Proposition 13
text: If a first magnitude has to a second the same ratio as a third to a fourth, and the third has to the fourth a greater ratio than a fifth has to a sixth, then the first also has to the second a greater ratio than the fifth to the sixth.

title: Book V, Proposition 14
text: If a first magnitude has to a second the same ratio as a third has to a fourth, and the first is greater than the third, then the second is also greater than the fourth; if equal, equal; and if less, less.

title: Book V, Proposition 15
text: Parts have the same ratio as their equimultiples.

title: Book V, Proposition 16
text: If four magnitudes are proportional, then they are also proportional alternately.

title: Book V, Proposition 17
text: If magnitudes are proportional taken jointly, then they are also proportional taken separately.

title: Book V, Proposition 18
text: If magnitudes are proportional taken separately, then they are also proportional taken jointly.

title: Book V, Proposition 19
text: If a whole is to a whole as a part subtracted is to a part subtracted, then the remainder is also to the remainder as the whole is to the whole.

title: Book V, Proposition 20
text: If there are three magnitudes, and others equal to them in multitude, which taken two and two are in the same ratio, and if ex aequali the first is greater than the third, then the fourth is also greater than the sixth; if equal, equal, and; if less, less.

title: Book V, Proposition 21
text: If there are three magnitudes, and others equal to them in multitude, which taken two and two together are in the same ratio, and the proportion of them is perturbed, then, if ex aequali the first magnitude is greater than the third, then the fourth is also greater than the sixth; if equal, equal; and if less, less.

title: Book V, Proposition 22
text: If there are any number of magnitudes whatever, and others equal to them in multitude, which taken two and two together are in the same ratio, then they are also in the same ratio ex aequali.

title: Book V, Proposition 23
text: If there are three magnitudes, and others equal to them in multitude, which taken two and two together are in the same ratio, and the proportion of them be perturbed, then they are also in the same ratio ex aequali.

title: Book V, Proposition 24
text: If a first magnitude has to a second the same ratio as a third has to a fourth, and also a fifth has to the second the same ratio as a sixth to the fourth, then the sum of the first and fifth has to the second the same ratio as the sum of the third and sixth has to the fourth.

title: Book V, Proposition 25
text: If four magnitudes are proportional, then the sum of the greatest and the least is greater than the sum of the remaining two.

title: Book VI, Proposition 1
text: Triangles and parallelograms which are under the same height are to one another as their bases.

title: Book VI, Proposition 2
text: If a straight line is drawn parallel to one of the sides of a triangle, then it cuts the sides of the triangle proportionally; and, if the sides of the triangle are cut proportionally, then the line joining the points of section is parallel to the remaining side of the triangle.

title: Book VI, Proposition 3
text: If an angle of a triangle is bisected by a straight line cutting the base, then the segments of the base have the same ratio as the remaining sides of the triangle; and, if segments of the base have the same ratio as the remaining sides of the triangle, then the straight line joining the vertex to the point of section bisects the angle of the triangle.

title: Book VI, Proposition 4
text: In equiangular triangles the sides about the equal angles are proportional where the corresponding sides are opposite the equal angles.

title: Book VI, Proposition 5
text: If two triangles have their sides proportional, then the triangles are equiangular with the equal angles opposite the corresponding sides.

title: Book VI, Proposition 6
text: If two triangles have one angle equal to one angle and the sides about the equal angles proportional, then the triangles are equiangular and have those angles equal opposite the corresponding sides.

title: Book VI, Proposition 7
text: If two triangles have one angle equal to one angle, the sides about other angles proportional, and the remaining angles either both less or both not less than a right angle, then the triangles are equiangular and have those angles equal the sides about which are proportional.

title: Book VI, Proposition 8
text: If in a right-angled triangle a perpendicular is drawn from the right angle to the base, then the triangles adjoining the perpendicular are similar both to the whole and to one another.

title: Book VI, Proposition 9
text: To cut off a prescribed part from a given straight line.

title: Book VI, Proposition 10
text: To cut a given uncut straight line similarly to a given cut straight line.

title: Book VI, Proposition 11
text: To find a third proportional to two given straight lines.

title: Book VI, Proposition 12
text: To find a fourth proportional to three given straight lines.

title: Book VI, Proposition 13
text: To find a mean proportional to two given straight lines.

title: Book VI, Proposition 14
text: In equal and equiangular parallelograms the sides about the equal angles are reciprocally proportional; and equiangular parallelograms in which the sides about the equal angles are reciprocally proportional are equal.

title: Book VI, Proposition 15
text: In equal triangles which have one angle equal to one angle the sides about the equal angles are reciprocally proportional; and those triangles which have one angle equal to one angle, and in which the sides about the equal angles are reciprocally proportional, are equal.

title: Book VI, Proposition 16
text: If four straight lines are proportional, then the rectangle contained by the extremes equals the rectangle contained by the means; and, if the rectangle contained by the extremes equals the rectangle contained by the means, then the four straight lines are proportional.

title: Book VI, Proposition 17
text: If three straight lines are proportional, then the rectangle contained by the extremes equals the square on the mean; and, if the rectangle contained by the extremes equals the square on the mean, then the three straight lines are proportional.

title: Book VI, Proposition 18
text: To describe a rectilinear figure similar and similarly situated to a given rectilinear figure on a given straight line.

title: Book VI, Proposition 19
text: Similar triangles are to one another in the duplicate ratio of the corresponding sides.

title: Book VI, Proposition 20
text: Similar polygons are divided into similar triangles, and into triangles equal in multitude and in the same ratio as the wholes, and the polygon has to the polygon a ratio duplicate of that which the corresponding side has to the corresponding side.

title: Book VI, Proposition 21
text: Figures which are similar to the same rectilinear figure are also similar to one another.

title: Book VI, Proposition 22
text: If four straight lines are proportional, then the rectilinear figures similar and similarly described upon them are also proportional; and, if the rectilinear figures similar and similarly described upon them are proportional, then the straight lines are themselves also proportional.

title: Book VI, Proposition 23
text: Equiangular parallelograms have to one another the ratio compounded of the ratios of their sides.

title: Book VI, Proposition 24
text: In any parallelogram the parallelograms about the diameter are similar both to the whole and to one another.

title: Book VI, Proposition 25
text: To construct a figure similar to one given rectilinear figure and equal to another.

title: Book VI, Proposition 26
text: If from a parallelogram there is taken away a parallelogram similar and similarly situated to the whole and having a common angle with it, then it is about the same diameter with the whole.

title: Book VI, Proposition 27
text: Of all the parallelograms applied to the same straight line falling short by parallelogrammic figures similar and similarly situated to that described on the half of the straight line, that parallelogram is greatest which is applied to the half of the straight line and is similar to the difference.

title: Book VI, Proposition 28
text: To apply a parallelogram equal to a given rectilinear figure to a given straight line but falling short by a parallelogram similar to a given one; thus the given rectilinear figure must not be greater than the parallelogram described on the half of the straight line and similar to the given parallelogram.

title: Book VI, Proposition 29
text: To apply a parallelogram equal to a given rectilinear figure to a given straight line but exceeding it by a parallelogram similar to a given one.

title: Book VI, Proposition 30
text: To cut a given finite straight line in extreme and mean ratio.

title: Book VI, Proposition 31
text: In right-angled triangles the figure on the side opposite the right angle equals the sum of the similar and similarly described figures on the sides containing the right angle.

title: Book VI, Proposition 32
text: If two triangles having two sides proportional to two sides are placed together at one angle so that their corresponding sides are also parallel, then the remaining sides of the triangles are in a straight line.

title: Book VI, Proposition 33
text: Angles in equal circles have the same ratio as the circumferences on which they stand whether they stand at the centers or at the circumferences.

title: Book VII, Proposition 1
text: When two unequal numbers are set out, and the less is continually subtracted in turn from the greater, if the number which is left never measures the one before it until a unit is left, then the original numbers are relatively prime.

title: Book VII, Proposition 2
text: To find the greatest common measure of two given numbers not relatively prime.

title: Book VII, Proposition 3
text: To find the greatest common measure of three given numbers not relatively prime.

title: Book VII, Proposition 4
text: Any number is either a part or parts of any number, the less of the greater.

title: Book VII, Proposition 5
text: If a number is part of a number, and another is the same part of another, then the sum is also the same part of the sum that the one is of the one.

title: Book VII, Proposition 6
text: If a number is parts of a number, and another is the same parts of another, then the sum is also the same parts of the sum that the one is of the one.

title: Book VII, Proposition 7
text: If a number is that part of a number which a subtracted number is of a subtracted number, then the remainder is also the same part of the remainder that the whole is of the whole.

title: Book VII, Proposition 8
text: If a number is the same parts of a number that a subtracted number is of a subtracted number, then the remainder is also the same parts of the remainder that the whole is of the whole.

title: Book VII, Proposition 9
text: If a number is a part of a number, and another is the same part of another, then alternately, whatever part or parts the first is of the third, the same part, or the same parts, the second is of the fourth.

title: Book VII, Proposition 10
text: If a number is a parts of a number, and another is the same parts of another, then alternately, whatever part of parts the first is of the third, the same part, or the same parts, the second is of the fourth.

title: Book VII, Proposition 11
text: If a whole is to a whole as a subtracted number is to a subtracted number, then the remainder is to the remainder as the whole is to the whole.

title: Book VII, Proposition 12
text: If any number of numbers are proportional, then one of the antecedents is to one of the consequents as the sum of the antecedents is to the sum of the consequents.

title: Book VII, Proposition 13
text: If four numbers are proportional, then they are also proportional alternately.

title: Book VII, Proposition 14
text: If there are any number of numbers, and others equal to them in multitude, which taken two and two together are in the same ratio, then they are also in the same ratio ex aequali.

title: Book VII, Proposition 15
text: If a unit number measures any number, and another number measures any other number the same number of times, then alternately, the unit measures the third number the same number of times that the second measures the fourth.

title: Book VII, Proposition 16
text: If two numbers multiplied by one another make certain numbers, then the numbers so produced equal one another.

title: Book VII, Proposition 17
text: If a number multiplied by two numbers makes certain numbers, then the numbers so produced have the same ratio as the numbers multiplied.

title: Book VII, Proposition 18
text: If two number multiplied by any number make certain numbers, then the numbers so produced have the same ratio as the multipliers.

title: Book VII, Proposition 19
text: If four numbers are proportional, then the number produced from the first and fourth equals the number produced from the second and third; and, if the number produced from the first and fourth equals that produced from the second and third, then the four numbers are proportional.

title: Book VII, Proposition 20
text: The least numbers of those which have the same ratio with them measure those which have the same ratio with them the same number of times; the greater the greater; and the less the less.

title: Book VII, Proposition 21
text: Numbers relatively prime are the least of those which have the same ratio with them.

title: Book VII, Proposition 22
text: The least numbers of those which have the same ratio with them are relatively prime.

title: Book VII, Proposition 23
text: If two numbers are relatively prime, then any number which measures one of them is relatively prime to the remaining number.

title: Book VII, Proposition 24
text: If two numbers are relatively prime to any number, then their product is also relatively prime to the same.

title: Book VII, Proposition 25
text: If two numbers are relatively prime, then the product of one of them with itself is relatively prime to the remaining one.

title: Book VII, Proposition 26
text: If two numbers are relatively prime to two numbers, both to each, then their products are also relatively prime.

title: Book VII, Proposition 27
text: If two numbers are relatively prime, and each multiplied by itself makes a certain number, then the products are relatively prime; and, if the original numbers multiplied by the products make certain numbers, then the latter are also relatively prime.

title: Book VII, Proposition 28
text: If two numbers are relatively prime, then their sum is also prime to each of them; and, if the sum of two numbers is relatively prime to either of them, then the original numbers are also relatively prime.

title: Book VII, Proposition 29
text: Any prime number is relatively prime to any number which it does not measure.

title: Book VII, Proposition 30
text: If two numbers, multiplied by one another make some number, and any prime number measures the product, then it also measures one of the original numbers.

title: Book VII, Proposition 31
text: Any composite number is measured by some prime number.

title: Book VII, Proposition 32
text: Any number is either prime or is measured by some prime number.

title: Book VII, Proposition 33
text: Given as many numbers as we please, to find the least of those which have the same ratio with them.

title: Book VII, Proposition 34
text: To find the least number which two given numbers measure.

title: Book VII, Proposition 35
text: If two numbers measure any number, then the least number measured by them also measures the same.

title: Book VII, Proposition 36
text: To find the least number which three given numbers measure.

title: Book VII, Proposition 37
text: If a number is measured by any number, then the number which is measured has a part called by the same name as the measuring number.

title: Book VII, Proposition 38
text: If a number has any part whatever, then it is measured by a number called by the same name as the part.

title: Book VII, Proposition 39
text: To find the number which is the least that has given parts.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 1
text: If there are as many numbers as we please in continued proportion, and the extremes of them are relatively prime, then the numbers are the least of those which have the same ratio with them.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 2
text: To find as many numbers as are prescribed in continued proportion, and the least that are in a given ratio.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 3
text: If as many numbers as we please in continued proportion are the least of those which have the same ratio with them, then the extremes of them are relatively prime.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 4
text: Given as many ratios as we please in least numbers, to find numbers in continued proportion which are the least in the given ratios.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 5
text: Plane numbers have to one another the ratio compounded of the ratios of their sides.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 6
text: If there are as many numbers as we please in continued proportion, and the first does not measure the second, then neither does any other measure any other.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 7
text: If there are as many numbers as we please in continued proportion, and the first measures the last, then it also measures the second.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 8
text: If between two numbers there fall numbers in continued proportion with them, then, however many numbers fall between them in continued proportion, so many also fall in continued proportion between the numbers which have the same ratios with the original numbers.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 9
text: If two numbers are relatively prime, and numbers fall between them in continued proportion, then, however many numbers fall between them in continued proportion, so many also fall between each of them and a unit in continued proportion.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 10
text: If numbers fall between two numbers and a unit in continued proportion, then however many numbers fall between each of them and a unit in continued proportion, so many also fall between the numbers themselves in continued proportion.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 11
text: Between two square numbers there is one mean proportional number, and the square has to the square the duplicate ratio of that which the side has to the side.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 12
text: Between two cubic numbers there are two mean proportional numbers, and the cube has to the cube the triplicate ratio of that which the side has to the side.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 13
text: If there are as many numbers as we please in continued proportion, and each multiplied by itself makes some number, then the products are proportional; and, if the original numbers multiplied by the products make certain numbers, then the latter are also proportional.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 14
text: If a square measures a square, then the side also measures the side; and, if the side measures the side, then the square also measures the square.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 15
text: If a cubic number measures a cubic number, then the side also measures the side; and, if the side measures the side, then the cube also measures the cube.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 16
text: If a square does not measure a square, then neither does the side measure the side; and, if the side does not measure the side, then neither does the square measure the square.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 17
text: If a cubic number does not measure a cubic number, then neither does the side measure the side; and, if the side does not measure the side, then neither does the cube measure the cube.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 18
text: Between two similar plane numbers there is one mean proportional number, and the plane number has to the plane number the ratio duplicate of that which the corresponding side has to the corresponding side.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 19
text: Between two similar solid numbers there fall two mean proportional numbers, and the solid number has to the solid number the ratio triplicate of that which the corresponding side has to the corresponding side.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 20
text: If one mean proportional number falls between two numbers, then the numbers are similar plane numbers.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 21
text: If two mean proportional numbers fall between two numbers, then the numbers are similar solid numbers.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 22
text: If three numbers are in continued proportion, and the first is square, then the third is also square.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 23
text: If four numbers are in continued proportion, and the first is a cube, then the fourth is also a cube.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 24
text: If two numbers have to one another the ratio which a square number has to a square number, and the first is square, then the second is also a square.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 25
text: If two numbers have to one another the ratio which a cubic number has to a cubic number, and the first is a cube, then the second is also a cube.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 26
text: Similar plane numbers have to one another the ratio which a square number has to a square number.

topic: Book VIII: Numbers in continued proportion
title: Book VIII, Proposition 27
text: Similar solid numbers have to one another the ratio which a cubic number has to a cubic number.

title: Book IX, Proposition 1
text: If two similar plane numbers multiplied by one another make some number, then the product is square.

title: Book IX, Proposition 2
text: If two numbers multiplied by one another make a square number, then they are similar plane numbers.

title: Book IX, Proposition 3
text: If a cubic number multiplied by itself makes some number, then the product is a cube.

title: Book IX, Proposition 4
text: If a cubic number multiplied by a cubic number makes some number, then the product is a cube.

title: Book IX, Proposition 5
text: If a cubic number multiplied by any number makes a cubic number, then the multiplied number is also cubic.

title: Book IX, Proposition 6
text: If a number multiplied by itself makes a cubic number, then it itself is also cubic.

title: Book IX, Proposition 7
text: If a composite number multiplied by any number makes some number, then the product is solid.

title: Book IX, Proposition 8
text: If as many numbers as we please beginning from a unit are in continued proportion, then the third from the unit is square as are also those which successively leave out one, the fourth is cubic as are also all those which leave out two, and the seventh is at once cubic and square are also those which leave out five.

title: Book IX, Proposition 9
text: If as many numbers as we please beginning from a unit are in continued proportion, and the number after the unit is square, then all the rest are also square; and if the number after the unit is cubic, then all the rest are also cubic.

title: Book IX, Proposition 10
text: If as many numbers as we please beginning from a unit are in continued proportion, and the number after the unit is not square, then neither is any other square except the third from the unit and all those which leave out one; and, if the number after the unit is not cubic, then neither is any other cubic except the fourth from the unit and all those which leave out two.

title: Book IX, Proposition 11
text: If as many numbers as we please beginning from a unit are in continued proportion, then the less measures the greater according to some one of the numbers which appear among the proportional numbers.

title: Book IX, Proposition 12
text: If as many numbers as we please beginning from a unit are in continued proportion, then by whatever prime numbers the last is measured, the next to the unit is also measured by the same.

title: Book IX, Proposition 13
text: If as many numbers as we please beginning from a unit are in continued proportion, and the number after the unit is prime, then the greatest is not measured by any except those which have a place among the proportional numbers.

title: Book IX, Proposition 14
text: If a number is the least that is measured by prime numbers, then it is not measured by any other prime number except those originally measuring it.

title: Book IX, Proposition 15
text: If three numbers in continued proportion are the least of those which have the same ratio with them, then the sum of any two is relatively prime to the remaining number.

title: Book IX, Proposition 16
text: If two numbers are relatively prime, then the second is not to any other number as the first is to the second.

title: Book IX, Proposition 17
text: If there are as many numbers as we please in continued proportion, and the extremes of them are relatively prime, then the last is not to any other number as the first is to the second.

title: Book IX, Proposition 18
text: Given two numbers, to investigate whether it is possible to find a third proportional to them.

title: Book IX, Proposition 19
text: Given three numbers, to investigate when it is possible to find a fourth proportional to them.

title: Book IX, Proposition 20
text: Prime numbers are more than any assigned multitude of prime numbers.

title: Book IX, Proposition 21
text: If as many even numbers as we please are added together, then the sum is even.

title: Book IX, Proposition 22
text: If as many odd numbers as we please are added together, and their multitude is even, then the sum is even.

title: Book IX, Proposition 23
text: If as many odd numbers as we please are added together, and their multitude is odd, then the sum is also odd.

title: Book IX, Proposition 24
text: If an even number is subtracted from an even number, then the remainder is even.

title: Book IX, Proposition 25
text: If an odd number is subtracted from an even number, then the remainder is odd.

title: Book IX, Proposition 26
text: If an odd number is subtracted from an odd number, then the remainder is even.

title: Book IX, Proposition 27
text: If an even number is subtracted from an odd number, then the remainder is odd.

title: Book IX, Proposition 28
text: If an odd number is multiplied by an even number, then the product is even.

title: Book IX, Proposition 29
text: If an odd number is multiplied by an odd number, then the product is odd.

title: Book IX, Proposition 30
text: If an odd number measures an even number, then it also measures half of it.

title: Book IX, Proposition 31
text: If an odd number is relatively prime to any number, then it is also relatively prime to double it.

title: Book IX, Proposition 32
text: Each of the numbers which are continually doubled beginning from a dyad is even-times even only.

title: Book IX, Proposition 33
text: If a number has its half odd, then it is even-times odd only.

title: Book IX, Proposition 34
text: If an [even] number neither is one of those which is continually doubled from a dyad, nor has its half odd, then it is both even-times even and even-times odd.

title: Book IX, Proposition 35
text: If as many numbers as we please are in continued proportion, and there is subtracted from the second and the last numbers equal to the first, then the excess of the second is to the first as the excess of the last is to the sum of all those before it.

title: Book IX, Proposition 36
text: If as many numbers as we please beginning from a unit are set out continuously in double proportion until the sum of all becomes prime, and if the sum multiplied into the last makes some number, then the product is perfect.

title: Book X, Proposition 1
text: Two unequal magnitudes being set out, if from the greater there is subtracted a magnitude greater than its half, and from that which is left a magnitude greater than its half, and if this process is repeated continually, then there will be left some magnitude less than the lesser magnitude set out. And the theorem can similarly be proven even if the parts subtracted are halves.

title: Book X, Proposition 2
text: If, when the less of two unequal magnitudes is continually subtracted in turn from the greater that which is left never measures the one before it, then the two magnitudes are incommensurable.

title: Book X, Proposition 3
text: To find the greatest common measure of two given commensurable magnitudes.

title: Book X, Proposition 4
text: To find the greatest common measure of three given commensurable magnitudes.

title: Book X, Proposition 5
text: Commensurable magnitudes have to one another the ratio which a number has to a number.

title: Book X, Proposition 6
text: If two magnitudes have to one another the ratio which a number has to a number, then the magnitudes are commensurable.

title: Book X, Proposition 7
text: Incommensurable magnitudes do not have to one another the ratio which a number has to a number.

title: Book X, Proposition 8
text: If two magnitudes do not have to one another the ratio which a number has to a number, then the magnitudes are incommensurable.

title: Book X, Proposition 9
text: The squares on straight lines commensurable in length have to one another the ratio which a square number has to a square number; and squares which have to one another the ratio which a square number has to a square number also have their sides commensurable in length. But the squares on straight lines incommensurable in length do not have to one another the ratio which a square number has to a square number; and squares which do not have to one another the ratio which a square number has to a square number also do not have their sides commensurable in length either.

title: Book X, Proposition 10
text: To find two straight lines incommensurable, the one in length only, and the other in square also, with an assigned straight line.

title: Book X, Proposition 11
text: If four magnitudes are proportional, and the first is commensurable with the second, then the third also is commensurable with the fourth; but, if the first is incommensurable with the second, then the third also is incommensurable with the fourth.

title: Book X, Proposition 12
text: Magnitudes commensurable with the same magnitude are also commensurable with one another.

title: Book X, Proposition 13
text: If two magnitudes are commensurable, and one of them is incommensurable with any magnitude, then the remaining one is also incommensurable with the same.

title: Book X, Proposition 14
text: Lemma. Given two unequal straight lines, to find by what square the square on the greater is greater than the square on the less. And, given two straight lines, to find the straight line the square on which equals the sum of the squares on them.

title: Book X, Proposition 15
text: If two commensurable magnitudes are added together, then the whole is also commensurable with each of them; and, if the whole is commensurable with one of them, then the original magnitudes are also commensurable.

title: Book X, Proposition 16
text: If two incommensurable magnitudes are added together, the sum is also incommensurable with each of them; but, if the sum is incommensurable with one of them, then the original magnitudes are also incommensurable.

title: Book X, Proposition 17
text: Lemma. If to any straight line there is applied a parallelogram but falling short by a square, then the applied parallelogram equals the rectangle contained by the segments of the straight line resulting from the application.

title: Book X, Proposition 18
text: If there are two unequal straight lines, and to the greater there is applied a parallelogram equal to the fourth part of the square on the less but falling short by a square, and if it divides it into incommensurable parts, then the square on the greater is greater than the square on the less by the square on a straight line incommensurable with the greater. And if the square on the greater is greater than the square on the less by the square on a straight line incommensurable with the greater, and if there is applied to the greater a parallelogram equal to the fourth part of the square on the less but falling short by a square, then it divides it into incommensurable parts.

title: Book X, Proposition 19
text: Lemma.

title: Book X, Proposition 20
text: If a rational area is applied to a rational straight line, then it produces as breadth a straight line rational and commensurable in length with the straight line to which it is applied.

title: Book X, Proposition 21
text: The rectangle contained by rational straight lines commensurable in square only is irrational, and the side of the square equal to it is irrational. Let the latter be called medial.

title: Book X, Proposition 22
text: Lemma. If there are two straight lines, then the first is to the second as the square on the first is to the rectangle contained by the two straight lines.

title: Book X, Proposition 23
text: A straight line commensurable with a medial straight line is medial.

title: Book X, Proposition 24
text: The rectangle contained by medial straight lines commensurable in length is medial.

title: Book X, Proposition 25
text: The rectangle contained by medial straight lines commensurable in square only is either rational or medial.

title: Book X, Proposition 26
text: A medial area does not exceed a medial area by a rational area.

title: Book X, Proposition 27
text: To find medial straight lines commensurable in square only which contain a rational rectangle.

title: Book X, Proposition 28
text: To find medial straight lines commensurable in square only which contain a medial rectangle.

title: Book X, Proposition 29
text: Lemma 1. To find two square numbers such that their sum is also square.

title: Book X, Proposition 30
text: To find two rational straight lines commensurable in square only such that the square on the greater is greater than the square on the less by the square on a straight line incommensurable in length with the greater.

title: Book X, Proposition 31
text: To find two medial straight lines commensurable in square only, containing a rational rectangle, such that the square on the greater is greater than the square on the less by the square on a straight line commensurable in length with the greater.

title: Book X, Proposition 32
text: To find two medial straight lines commensurable in square only, containing a medial rectangle, such that the square on the greater is greater than the square on the less by the square on a straight line commensurable with the greater.

title: Book X, Proposition 33
text: Lemma.

title: Book X, Proposition 34
text: To find two straight lines incommensurable in square which make the sum of the squares on them medial but the rectangle contained by them rational.

title: Book X, Proposition 35
text: To find two straight lines incommensurable in square which make the sum of the squares on them medial and the rectangle contained by them medial and moreover incommensurable with the sum of the squares on them.

title: Book X, Proposition 36
text: If two rational straight lines commensurable in square only are added together, then the whole is irrational; let it be called binomial.

title: Book X, Proposition 37
text: If two medial straight lines commensurable in square only and containing a rational rectangle are added together, the whole is irrational; let it be called the first bimedial straight line.

title: Book X, Proposition 38
text: If two medial straight lines commensurable in square only and containing a medial rectangle are added together, then the whole is irrational; let it be called the second bimedial straight line.

title: Book X, Proposition 39
text: If two straight lines incommensurable in square which make the sum of the squares on them rational but the rectangle contained by them medial are added together, then the whole straight line is irrational; let it be called major.

title: Book X, Proposition 40
text: If two straight lines incommensurable in square which make the sum of the squares on them medial but the rectangle contained by them rational are added together, then the whole straight line is irrational; let it be called the side of a rational plus a medial area.

title: Book X, Proposition 41
text: If two straight lines incommensurable in square which make the sum of the squares on them medial and the rectangle contained by them medial and also incommensurable with the sum of the squares on them are added together, then the whole straight line is irrational; let it be called the side of the sum of two medial areas.

title: Book X, Proposition 42
text: A binomial straight line is divided into its terms at one point only.

title: Book X, Proposition 43
text: A first bimedial straight line is divided at one and the same point only.

title: Book X, Proposition 44
text: A second bimedial straight line is divided at one point only.

title: Book X, Proposition 45
text: A major straight line is divided at one point only.

title: Book X, Proposition 46
text: The side of a rational plus a medial area is divided at one point only.

title: Book X, Proposition 47
text: The side of the sum of two medial areas is divided at one point only.

title: Book X, Proposition 48
text: To find the first binomial line.

title: Book X, Proposition 49
text: To find the second binomial line.

title: Book X, Proposition 50
text: To find the third binomial line.

title: Book X, Proposition 51
text: To find the fourth binomial line.

title: Book X, Proposition 52
text: To find the fifth binomial line.

title: Book X, Proposition 53
text: To find the sixth binomial line.

title: Book X, Proposition 54
text: Lemma.

title: Book X, Proposition 55
text: If an area is contained by a rational straight line and the second binomial, then the side of the area is the irrational straight line which is called a first bimedial.

title: Book X, Proposition 56
text: If an area is contained by a rational straight line and the third binomial, then the side of the area is the irrational straight line called a second bimedial.

title: Book X, Proposition 57
text: If an area is contained by a rational straight line and the fourth binomial, then the side of the area is the irrational straight line called major.

title: Book X, Proposition 58
text: If an area is contained by a rational straight line and the fifth binomial, then the side of the area is the irrational straight line called the side of a rational plus a medial area.

title: Book X, Proposition 59
text: If an area is contained by a rational straight line and the sixth binomial, then the side of the area is the irrational straight line called the side of the sum of two medial areas.

title: Book X, Proposition 60
text: Lemma. If a straight line is cut into unequal parts, then the sum of the squares on the unequal parts is greater than twice the rectangle contained by the unequal parts.

title: Book X, Proposition 61
text: The square on the first bimedial straight line applied to a rational straight line produces as breadth the second binomial.

title: Book X, Proposition 62
text: The square on the second bimedial straight line applied to a rational straight line produces as breadth the third binomial.

title: Book X, Proposition 63
text: The square on the major straight line applied to a rational straight line produces as breadth the fourth binomial.

title: Book X, Proposition 64
text: The square on the side of a rational plus a medial area applied to a rational straight line produces as breadth the fifth binomial.

title: Book X, Proposition 65
text: The square on the side of the sum of two medial areas applied to a rational straight line produces as breadth the sixth binomial.

title: Book X, Proposition 66
text: A straight line commensurable with a binomial straight line is itself also binomial and the same in order.

title: Book X, Proposition 67
text: A straight line commensurable with a bimedial straight line is itself also bimedial and the same in order.

title: Book X, Proposition 68
text: A straight line commensurable with a major straight line is itself also major.

title: Book X, Proposition 69
text: A straight line commensurable with the side of a rational plus a medial area is itself also the side of a rational plus a medial area.

title: Book X, Proposition 70
text: A straight line commensurable with the side of the sum of two medial areas is the side of the sum of two medial areas.

title: Book X, Proposition 71
text: If a rational and a medial are added together, then four irrational straight lines arise, namely a binomial or a first bimedial or a major or a side of a rational plus a medial area.

title: Book X, Proposition 72
text: If two medial areas incommensurable with one another are added together, then the remaining two irrational straight lines arise, namely either a second bimedial or a side of the sum of two medial areas.

title: Book X, Proposition 73
text: If from a rational straight line there is subtracted a rational straight line commensurable with the whole in square only, then the remainder is irrational; let it be called an apotome.

title: Book X, Proposition 74
text: If from a medial straight line there is subtracted a medial straight line which is commensurable with the whole in square only, and which contains with the whole a rational rectangle, then the remainder is irrational; let it be called first apotome of a medial straight line.

title: Book X, Proposition 75
text: If from a medial straight line there is subtracted a medial straight line which is commensurable with the whole in square only, and which contains with the whole a medial rectangle, then the remainder is irrational; let it be called second apotome of a medial straight line.

title: Book X, Proposition 76
text: If from a straight line there is subtracted a straight line which is incommensurable in square with the whole and which with the whole makes the sum of the squares on them added together rational, but the rectangle contained by them medial, then the remainder is irrational; let it be called minor.

title: Book X, Proposition 77
text: If from a straight line there is subtracted a straight line which is incommensurable in square with the whole, and which with the whole makes the sum of the squares on them medial but twice the rectangle contained by them rational, then the remainder is irrational; let it be called that which produces with a rational area a medial whole.

title: Book X, Proposition 78
text: If from a straight line there is subtracted a straight line which is incommensurable in square with the whole and which with the whole makes the sum of the squares on them medial, twice the rectangle contained by them medial, and further the squares on them incommensurable with twice the rectangle contained by them, then the remainder is irrational; let it be called that which produces with a medial area a medial whole.

title: Book X, Proposition 79
text: To an apotome only one rational straight line can be annexed which is commensurable with the whole in square only.

title: Book X, Proposition 80
text: To a first apotome of a medial straight line only one medial straight line can be annexed which is commensurable with the whole in square only and which contains with the whole a rational rectangle.

title: Book X, Proposition 81
text: To a second apotome of a medial straight line only one medial straight line can be annexed which is commensurable with the whole in square only and which contains with the whole a medial rectangle.

title: Book X, Proposition 82
text: To a minor straight line only one straight line can be annexed which is incommensurable in square with the whole and which makes, with the whole, the sum of squares on them rational but twice the rectangle contained by them medial.

title: Book X, Proposition 83
text: To a straight line which produces with a rational area a medial whole only one straight line can be annexed which is incommensurable in square with the whole straight line and which with the whole straight line makes the sum of squares on them medial but twice the rectangle contained by them rational.

title: Book X, Proposition 84
text: To a straight line which produces with a medial area a medial whole only one straight line can be annexed which is incommensurable in square with the whole straight line and which with the whole straight line makes the sum of squares on them medial and twice the rectangle contained by them both medial and also incommensurable with the sum of the squares on them.

title: Book X, Proposition 91
text: If an area is contained by a rational straight line and a first apotome, then the side of the area is an apotome.

title: Book X, Proposition 92
text: If an area is contained by a rational straight line and a second apotome, then the side of the area is a first apotome of a medial straight line.

title: Book X, Proposition 93
text: If an area is contained by a rational straight line and a third apotome, then the side of the area is a second apotome of a medial straight line.
