title: Book X, Proposition 96
text: If an area is contained by a rational straight line and a sixth apotome, then the side of the area is a straight line which produces with a medial area a medial whole.

title: Book X, Proposition 97
text: The square on an apotome of a medial straight line applied to a rational straight line produces as breadth a first apotome.

title: Book X, Proposition 98
text: The square on a first apotome of a medial straight line applied to a rational straight line produces as breadth a second apotome.

title: Book X, Proposition 99
text: The square on a second apotome of a medial straight line applied to a rational straight line produces as breadth a third apotome.

title: Book X, Proposition 100
text: The square on a minor straight line applied to a rational straight line produces as breadth a fourth apotome.

title: Book X, Proposition 101
text: The square on the straight line which produces with a rational area a medial whole, if applied to a rational straight line, produces as breadth a fifth apotome.

title: Book X, Proposition 102
text: The square on the straight line which produces with a medial area a medial whole, if applied to a rational straight line, produces as breadth a sixth apotome.

title: Book X, Proposition 103
text: A straight line commensurable in length with an apotome is an apotome and the same in order.

title: Book X, Proposition 104
text: A straight line commensurable with an apotome of a medial straight line is an apotome of a medial straight line and the same in order.

title: Book X, Proposition 105
text: A straight line commensurable with a minor straight line is minor.

title: Book X, Proposition 106
text: A straight line commensurable with that which produces with a rational area a medial whole is a straight line which produces with a rational area a medial whole.

title: Book X, Proposition 107
text: A straight line commensurable with that which produces a medial area and a medial whole is itself also a straight line which produces with a medial area a medial whole.

title: Book X, Proposition 108
text: If from a rational area a medial area is subtracted, the side of the remaining area becomes one of two irrational straight lines, either an apotome or a minor straight line.

title: Book X, Proposition 109
text: If from a medial area a rational area is subtracted, then there arise two other irrational straight lines, either a first apotome of a medial straight line or a straight line which produces with a rational area a medial whole.

title: Book X, Proposition 110
text: If from a medial area there is subtracted a medial area incommensurable with the whole, then the two remaining irrational straight lines arise, either a second apotome of a medial straight line or a straight line which produce with a medial area a medial whole.

title: Book X, Proposition 111
text: The apotome is not the same with the binomial straight line.

title: Book X, Proposition 112
text: The square on a rational straight line applied to the binomial straight line produces as breadth an apotome the terms of which are commensurable with the terms of the binomial straight line and moreover in the same ratio; and further the apotome so arising has the same order as the binomial straight line.

title: Book X, Proposition 113
text: The square on a rational straight line, if applied to an apotome, produces as breadth the binomial straight line the terms of which are commensurable with the terms of the apotome and in the same ratio; and further the binomial so arising has the same order as the apotome.

title: Book X, Proposition 114
text: If an area is contained by an apotome and the binomial straight line the terms of which are commensurable with the terms of the apotome and in the same ratio, then the side of the area is rational.

title: Book X, Proposition 115
text: From a medial straight line there arise irrational straight lines infinite in number, and none of them is the same as any preceding.

title: Book XI, Proposition 1
text: A part of a straight line cannot be in the plane of reference and a part in plane more elevated.

title: Book XI, Proposition 2
text: If two straight lines cut one another, then they lie in one plane; and every triangle lies in one plane.

title: Book XI, Proposition 3
text: If two planes cut one another, then their intersection is a straight line.

title: Book XI, Proposition 4
text: If a straight line is set up at right angles to two straight lines which cut one another at their common point of section, then it is also at right angles to the plane passing through them.

title: Book XI, Proposition 5
text: If a straight line is set up at right angles to three straight lines which meet one another at their common point of section, then the three straight lines lie in one plane.

title: Book XI, Proposition 6
text: If two straight lines are at right angles to the same plane, then the straight lines are parallel.

title: Book XI, Proposition 7
text: If two straight lines are parallel and points are taken at random on each of them, then the straight line joining the points is in the same plane with the parallel straight lines.

title: Book XI, Proposition 8
text: If two straight lines are parallel, and one of them is at right angles to any plane, then the remaining one is also at right angles to the same plane.

title: Book XI, Proposition 9
text: Straight lines which are parallel to the same straight line but do not lie in the same plane with it are also parallel to each other.

title: Book XI, Proposition 10
text: If two straight lines meeting one another are parallel to two straight lines meeting one another not in the same plane, then they contain equal angles.

title: Book XI, Proposition 11
text: To draw a straight line perpendicular to a given plane from a given elevated point.

title: Book XI, Proposition 12
text: To set up a straight line at right angles to a give plane from a given point in it.

title: Book XI, Proposition 13
text: From the same point two straight lines cannot be set up at right angles to the same plane on the same side.

title: Book XI, Proposition 14
text: Planes to which the same straight line is at right angles are parallel.

title: Book XI, Proposition 15
text: If two straight lines meeting one another are parallel to two straight lines meeting one another not in the same plane, then the planes through them are parallel.

title: Book XI, Proposition 16
text: If two parallel planes are cut by any plane, then their intersections are parallel.

title: Book XI, Proposition 17
text: If two straight lines are cut by parallel planes, then they are cut in the same ratios.

title: Book XI, Proposition 18
text: If a straight line is at right angles to any plane, then all the planes through it are also at right angles to the same plane.

title: Book XI, Proposition 19
text: If two planes which cut one another are at right angles to any plane, then their intersection is also at right angles to the same plane.

title: Book XI, Proposition 20
text: If a solid angle is contained by three plane angles, then the sum of any two is greater than the remaining one.

title: Book XI, Proposition 21
text: Any solid angle is contained by plane angles whose sum is less than four right angles.

title: Book XI, Proposition 22
text: If there are three plane angles such that the sum of any two is greater than the remaining one, and they are contained by equal straight lines, then it is possible to construct a triangle out of the straight lines joining the ends of the equal straight lines.

title: Book XI, Proposition 23
text: To construct a solid angles out of three plane angles such that the sum of any two is greater than the remaining one: thus the sum of the three angles must be less than four right angles.

title: Book XI, Proposition 24
text: If a solid is contained by parallel planes, then the opposite planes in it are equal and parallelogrammic.

title: Book XI, Proposition 25
text: If a parallelepipedal solid is cut by a plane parallel to the opposite planes, then the base is to the base as the solid is to the solid.

title: Book XI, Proposition 26
text: To construct a solid angle equal to a given solid angle on a given straight line at a given point on it.

title: Book XI, Proposition 27
text: To describe a parallelepipedal solid similar and similarly situated to a given parallelepipedal solid on a given straight line.

title: Book XI, Proposition 28
text: If a parallelepipedal solid is cut by a plane through the diagonals of the opposite planes, then the solid is bisected by the plane.

title: Book XI, Proposition 29
text: Parallelepipedal solids which are on the same base and of the same height, and in which the ends of their edges which stand up are on the same straight lines, equal one another.

title: Book XI, Proposition 30
text: Parallelepipedal solids which are on the same base and of the same height, and in which the ends of their edges which stand up are not on the same straight lines, equal one another.

title: Book XI, Proposition 31
text: Parallelepipedal solids which are on equal bases and of the same height equal one another.

title: Book XI, Proposition 32
text: Parallelepipedal solids which are of the same height are to one another as their bases.

title: Book XI, Proposition 33
text: Similar parallelepipedal solids are to one another in the triplicate ratio of their corresponding sides.

title: Book XI, Proposition 34
text: In equal parallelepipedal solids the bases are reciprocally proportional to the heights; and those parallelepipedal solids in which the bases are reciprocally proportional to the heights are equal.

title: Book XI, Proposition 35
text: If there are two equal plane angles, and on their vertices there are set up elevated straight lines containing equal angles with the original straight lines respectively, if on the elevated straight lines points are taken at random and perpendiculars are drawn from them to the planes in which the original angles are, and if from the points so arising in the planes straight lines are joined to the vertices of the original angles, then they contain with the elevated straight lines equal angles.

title: Book XI, Proposition 36
text: If three straight lines are proportional, then the parallelepipedal solid formed out of the three equals the parallelepipedal solid on the mean which is equilateral, but equiangular with the aforesaid solid.

title: Book XI, Proposition 37
text: If four straight lines are proportional, then parallelepipedal solids on them which are similar and similarly described are also proportional; and, if the parallelepipedal solids on them which are similar and similarly described are proportional, then the straight lines themselves are also proportional.

title: Book XI, Proposition 38
text: If the sides of the opposite planes of a cube are bisected, and the planes are carried through the points of section, then the intersection of the planes and the diameter of the cube bisect one another.

title: Book XI, Proposition 39
text: If there are two prisms of equal height, and one has a parallelogram as base and the other a triangle, and if the parallelogram is double the triangle, then the prisms are equal.

topic: Book XII: Areas and volumes by exhaustion
title: Book XII, Proposition 1
text: Similar polygons inscribed in circles are to one another as the squares on their diameters.

topic: Book XII: Areas and volumes by exhaustion
title: Book XII, Proposition 2
text: Circles are to one another as the squares on their diameters.

topic: Book XII: Areas and volumes by exhaustion
title: Book XII, Proposition 3

title: Book XII, Proposition 4

topic: Book XII: Areas and volumes by exhaustion
title: Book XII, Proposition 5
text: Pyramids of the same height with triangular bases are to one another as their bases.

topic: Book XII: Areas and volumes by exhaustion
title: Book XII, Proposition 6
text: Pyramids of the same height with polygonal bases are to one another as their bases.

topic: Book XII: Areas and volumes by exhaustion
title: Book XII, Proposition 7

topic: Book XII: Areas and volumes by exhaustion
title: Book XII, Proposition 8
text: Similar pyramids with triangular bases are in triplicate ratio of their corresponding sides.

topic: Book XII: Areas and volumes by exhaustion
title: Book XII, Proposition 9

topic: Book XII: Areas and volumes by exhaustion
title: Book XII, Proposition 10
text: Any cone is a third part of the cylinder with the same base and equal height.

topic: Book XII: Areas and volumes by exhaustion
title: Book XII, Proposition 11
text: Cones and cylinders of the same height are to one another as their bases.

topic: Book XII: Areas and volumes by exhaustion
title: Book XII, Proposition 12
text: Similar cones and cylinders are to one another in triplicate ratio of the diameters of their bases.

topic: Book XII: Areas and volumes by exhaustion
title: Book XII, Proposition 13

topic: Book XII: Areas and volumes by exhaustion
title: Book XII, Proposition 14
text: Cones and cylinders on equal bases are to one another as their heights.

topic: Book XII: Areas and volumes by exhaustion
title: Book XII, Proposition 15
text: In equal cones and cylinders the bases are reciprocally proportional to the heights; and those cones and cylinders in which the bases are reciprocally proportional to the heights are equal.

topic: Book XII: Areas and volumes by exhaustion
title: Book XII, Proposition 16

topic: Book XII: Areas and volumes by exhaustion
title: Book XII, Proposition 18
text: Spheres are to one another in triplicate ratio of their respective diameters.

title: Book XIII, Proposition 1
text: If a straight line is cut in extreme and mean ratio, then the square on the greater segment added to the half of the whole is five times the square on the half.

title: Book XIII, Proposition 2
text: If the square on a straight line is five times the square on a segment on it, then, when the double of the said segment is cut in extreme and mean ratio, the greater segment is the remaining part of the original straight line.

title: Book XIII, Proposition 3
text: If a straight line is cut in extreme and mean ratio, then the square on the sum of the lesser segment and the half of the greater segment is five times the square on the half of the greater segment.

title: Book XIII, Proposition 4
text: If a straight line is cut in extreme and mean ratio, then the sum of the squares on the whole and on the lesser segment is triple the square on the greater segment.

title: Book XIII, Proposition 5
text: If a straight line is cut in extreme and mean ratio, and a straight line equal to the greater segment is added to it, then the whole straight line has been cut in extreme and mean ratio, and the original straight line is the greater segment.

title: Book XIII, Proposition 6
text: If a rational straight line is cut in extreme and mean ratio, then each of the segments is the irrational straight line called apotome.

title: Book XIII, Proposition 7
text: If three angles of an equilateral pentagon, taken either in order or not in order, are equal, then the pentagon is equiangular.

title: Book XIII, Proposition 8
text: If in an equilateral and equiangular pentagon straight lines subtend two angles are taken in order, then they cut one another in extreme and mean ratio, and their greater segments equal the side of the pentagon.

title: Book XIII, Proposition 9
text: If the side of the hexagon and that of the decagon inscribed in the same circle are added together, then the whole straight line has been cut in extreme and mean ratio, and its greater segment is the side of the hexagon.

title: Book XIII, Proposition 10
text: If an equilateral pentagon is inscribed ina circle, then the square on the side of the pentagon equals the sum of the squares on the sides of the hexagon and the decagon inscribed in the same circle.

title: Book XIII, Proposition 11
text: If an equilateral pentagon is inscribed in a circle which has its diameter rational, then the side of the pentagon is the irrational straight line called minor.

title: Book XIII, Proposition 12
text: If an equilateral triangle is inscribed in a circle, then the square on the side of the triangle is triple the square on the radius of the circle.

title: Book XIII, Proposition 13
text: To construct a pyramid, to comprehend it in a given sphere; and to prove that the square on the diameter of the sphere is one and a half times the square on the side of the pyramid.

title: Book XIII, Proposition 14
text: To construct an octahedron and comprehend it in a sphere, as in the preceding case; and to prove that the square on the diameter of the sphere is double the square on the side of the octahedron.

title: Book XIII, Proposition 15
text: To construct a cube and comprehend it in a sphere, like the pyramid; and to prove that the square on the diameter of the sphere is triple the square on the side of the cube.

title: Book XIII, Proposition 16
text: To construct an icosahedron and comprehend it in a sphere, like the aforesaid figures; and to prove that the square on the side of the icosahedron is the irrational straight line called minor.

title: Book XIII, Proposition 17
text: To construct a dodecahedron and comprehend it in a sphere, like the aforesaid figures; and to prove that the square on the side of the dodecahedron is the irrational straight line called apotome.

title: Book XIII, Proposition 18
text: To set out the sides of the five figures and compare them with one another.
